records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: a last speech, added after the blessings and curses
decisions.reason: Chapter 26 closed with a summary (26:46), and this chapter has a summary of its own (verse 34). It deals with gifts promised to the LORD by vow and with what already belongs to him, firstborn animals and tithes, and how each may or may not be bought back.

records.heading: Vows of people

records.source: דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אִ֕ישׁ כִּ֥י יַפְלִ֖א נֶ֑דֶר בְּעֶרְכְּךָ֥ נְפָשֹׁ֖ת לַֽיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel and say to them: a man, when he makes extraordinary a vow by your valuation of persons to Yahweh,
pieces: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them: 'When {{gender:anyone|any man}} makes a special vow to give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the value of a person,

L.2: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and say to them, '{{gender:A person|A man}}, when he makes a special vow by your valuation of persons to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},

R.2: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'Someone may make a special promise to give a person to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then they are to pay the set price for that person.

decisions.choice: makes a special vow: a vow out of the ordinary
decisions.reason: The verb means to do something remarkable or beyond the usual. With "vow" it describes a solemn, uncommon promise, here the promise of a person to the LORD. The same phrase opens the Nazirite vow (Numbers 6:2). A vow was a promise to give God something, often in return for help asked of him (Genesis 28:20-22; 1 Samuel 1:11).

decisions.choice: your valuation of persons: the fixed price of a person, paid in silver
decisions.reason: The word means an assessment or set value. Its ending "your" is fixed in this formula through the whole chapter and is never explained; it may once have addressed Moses or the priest, but it works as a technical term, "the valuation". The person vowed (oneself or a member of the household) was not handed over to the sanctuary; the vow was kept by paying the value set out in verses 3-7. Hannah's gift of Samuel to serve at the sanctuary (1 Samuel 1:11, 28) shows the other way such a vow could be kept.

decisions.choice: a man: anyone who vows, man or woman
decisions.reason: The word is "man", but the law covers anyone who makes such a vow; Numbers 30 deals with the vows of women. The valuations that follow are set by the sex and age of the person vowed, not of the one who makes the vow.

decisions.choice: the value of a person / the set price
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out the fixed "your", which in this phrase names no particular person, and say what the valuation is. Literal keeps "your valuation" through the chapter.

decisions.choice: Then they are to pay the set price for that person.
decisions.reason: Readable states outright what verse 3 implies: the person vowed is released by paying the value that follows. Literal and Balanced leave the sentence open into verse 3.

records.source: וְהָיָ֤ה עֶרְכְּךָ֙ הַזָּכָ֔ר מִבֶּן֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְעַ֖ד בֶּן־שִׁשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה וְהָיָ֣ה עֶרְכְּךָ֗ חֲמִשִּׁ֛ים שֶׁ֥קֶל כֶּ֖סֶף בְּשֶׁ֥קֶל הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: And will be your valuation of the male from a son of twenty year[s] and to a son of sixty year[s], and will be your valuation fifty shekel[s] of silver by [the] shekel of the holy place.
pieces: the valuation for a man from twenty to sixty years of age is to be fifty shekels of silver, measured by the sanctuary shekel.

L.3: then your valuation of the male from twenty years old up to sixty years old shall be — your valuation shall be fifty shekels of silver, by the shekel of the sanctuary.

R.3: For a man between twenty and sixty years old, the set price is fifty shekels of silver, weighed by the official shekel used at the holy tent.

decisions.choice: shekels of silver: a weight of silver, not a coin
decisions.reason: The shekel was a unit of weight, about 11.5 grams or two-fifths of an ounce. Coins were not yet in use; silver was weighed out (Genesis 23:16; Jeremiah 32:9-10). Fifty shekels was about 20 ounces of silver. For comparison, the law sets thirty shekels as the price of a slave (Exodus 21:32), and fifty shekels is the sum paid in Deuteronomy 22:29.

decisions.choice: by the shekel of the holy place: by the standard sanctuary weight
decisions.reason: Weights could differ from place to place. "The shekel of the holy place" was the official standard used for payments to the sanctuary, fixed at twenty gerahs (verse 25; Exodus 30:13), as in 5:15.

decisions.choice: the male from twenty to sixty: the first of four age groups
decisions.reason: The values in verses 3-7 are set by sex and by age: twenty to sixty, five to twenty, one month to five years, and over sixty. Twenty is the age at which men were counted for the army and paid the half shekel (Exodus 30:14; Numbers 1:3). The text does not explain how the amounts were fixed; they are the prices for releasing a vow, not a measure of a person's worth before God.

decisions.choice: shall be — your valuation shall be
decisions.reason: The Hebrew starts the sentence, breaks off after the age range, and starts again with "your valuation shall be". Literal shows the restart with a dash; Balanced and Readable say it once.

decisions.choice: measured by
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "measured" to make clear that the sanctuary shekel is the standard weight for the payment. Readable says "weighed by".

records.source: וְאִם־נְקֵבָ֖ה הִ֑וא וְהָיָ֥ה עֶרְכְּךָ֖ שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים שָֽׁקֶל׃
records.gloss: And if [a] female she [is], and will be your valuation thirty shekel[s].
pieces: If it is a woman, the valuation is thirty shekels.

L.4: And if she [is] a female, then your valuation shall be thirty shekels.

R.4: For a woman, the set price is thirty shekels.

decisions.choice: a female of the same age: twenty to sixty
decisions.reason: The verse continues verse 3: a woman in the same age group is valued at thirty shekels of silver by the sanctuary shekel.

decisions.choice: a woman
decisions.reason: In this age group the "female" is a grown woman, as the "male" in verse 3 is a man. The word itself means female and is kept at Literal.

records.source: וְאִ֨ם מִבֶּן־חָמֵ֜שׁ שָׁנִ֗ים וְעַד֙ בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְהָיָ֧ה עֶרְכְּךָ֛ הַזָּכָ֖ר עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שְׁקָלִ֑ים וְלַנְּקֵבָ֖ה עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת שְׁקָלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And if from a son of five years and to a son of twenty year[s], and will be your valuation of the male twenty shekels, and for the female ten shekels.
pieces: For someone from five to twenty years of age, the valuation is twenty shekels for a male and ten shekels for a female.

L.5: And if [the person is] from five years old up to twenty years old, then your valuation of the male shall be twenty shekels, and for the female ten shekels.

R.5: For a boy or girl between five and twenty years old, the set price is twenty shekels for a boy and ten shekels for a girl.

decisions.choice: from five to twenty: the second age group
decisions.reason: "A son of five years" is the Hebrew way of saying "five years old"; it covers both sexes here, as the verse goes on to name male and female.

decisions.choice: a boy ... a girl
decisions.reason: In this age group Readable says "boy" and "girl" for "male" and "female", though the oldest are young adults.

records.source: וְאִ֣ם מִבֶּן־חֹ֗דֶשׁ וְעַד֙ בֶּן־חָמֵ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים וְהָיָ֤ה עֶרְכְּךָ֙ הַזָּכָ֔ר חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה שְׁקָלִ֖ים כָּ֑סֶף וְלַנְּקֵבָ֣ה עֶרְכְּךָ֔ שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת שְׁקָלִ֖ים כָּֽסֶף׃
records.gloss: And if from a son of a month and to a son of five years, and will be your valuation of the male five shekels of silver, and for the female your valuation three shekels of silver.
pieces: For a child from one month to five years old, the valuation is five shekels of silver for a male and three shekels of silver for a female.

L.6: And if [the person is] from a month old up to five years old, then your valuation of the male shall be five shekels of silver, and for the female your valuation [shall be] three shekels of silver.

R.6: For a child between one month and five years old, the set price is five shekels of silver for a boy and three shekels of silver for a girl.

decisions.choice: from a month: from the age of one month
decisions.reason: A child younger than a month was not counted; the firstborn son was redeemed at one month for five shekels (Numbers 3:15; 18:16), the same amount set here for a boy.

records.source: וְ֠אִם מִבֶּן־שִׁשִּׁ֨ים שָׁנָ֤ה וָמַ֨עְלָה֙ אִם־זָכָ֔ר וְהָיָ֣ה עֶרְכְּךָ֔ חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר שָׁ֑קֶל וְלַנְּקֵבָ֖ה עֲשָׂרָ֥ה שְׁקָלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And if from a son of sixty year[s] and upward, if [a] male, and will be your valuation fifteen shekel[s], and for the female ten shekels.
pieces: For someone sixty years old or more, the valuation is fifteen shekels for a man and ten shekels for a woman.

L.7: And if [the person is] from sixty years old and upward, if a male, then your valuation shall be fifteen shekels, and for the female ten shekels.

R.7: For a person over sixty years old, the set price is fifteen shekels for a man and ten shekels for a woman.

decisions.choice: from sixty upward: the oldest age group
decisions.reason: The values fall for those over sixty, more for men (from fifty to fifteen shekels) than for women (from thirty to ten).

records.source: וְאִם־מָ֥ךְ הוּא֙ מֵֽעֶרְכֶּ֔ךָ וְהֶֽעֱמִידוֹ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהֶעֱרִ֥יךְ אֹת֖וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֑ן עַל־פִּ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר תַּשִּׂיג֙ יַ֣ד הַנֹּדֵ֔ר יַעֲרִיכֶ֖נּוּ הַכֹּהֵֽן׃ס
records.gloss: And if [too] poor he [is] for your valuation, and he will station him before the priest, and will value him the priest; according to the mouth of what will reach [the] hand of the one vowing will value him the priest.
pieces: But if the one who vows is too poor to pay the valuation, the person is to be brought before the priest, and the priest will set a value for them, fixing the amount by what the one who vowed is able to pay.

L.8: But if he is too poor for your valuation, then he shall set him before the priest, and the priest shall value him; according to what the hand of the one who vowed can reach, the priest shall value him.

R.8: But someone may be too poor to pay the set price. Then the person who was promised must be brought to the priest. The priest will decide on a price that the one who made the promise is able to pay.

decisions.choice: he ... him: the one who vowed brings the person vowed
decisions.reason: "He" who is too poor is the one who made the vow. "Him" whom he sets before the priest is most likely the person vowed, who may be the vower himself. The verb "set" is literally "make stand", to present someone formally.

decisions.choice: what the hand can reach: what the person can afford
decisions.reason: "His hand reaches" means he has the means for something, as in 5:7, 11; 14:21-22, 30-32 for the poor who bring smaller offerings. The vow is not cancelled but scaled to the vower's means.

decisions.choice: the one who vows / the person
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who is meant by each "he" and "him", following m1. Literal keeps the pronouns.

records.source: וְאִם־בְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַקְרִ֧יבוּ מִמֶּ֛נָּה קָרְבָּ֖ן לַֽיהוָ֑ה כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִתֵּ֥ן מִמֶּ֛נּוּ לַיהוָ֖ה יִֽהְיֶה־קֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: And if an animal which people bring near of it [as] an offering to Yahweh, all that he gives of it to Yahweh will be holy.
pieces: If the vow is of an animal of the kind that may be presented as an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, any such animal given to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} becomes holy.

L.9: And if [it is] an animal of which [people] bring near an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all that he gives of it to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shall be holy.

R.9: Someone may promise an animal of a kind that can be offered to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Any animal given to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in this way becomes holy.

decisions.choice: an animal that may be brought as an offering: a clean animal fit for the altar
decisions.reason: Cattle, sheep and goats could be offered (1:2); unclean animals could not (verse 11). An offering here is the general word for what is brought near to the LORD, as in 1:2.

decisions.choice: will be holy: it now belongs to the LORD and cannot be taken back
decisions.reason: Once vowed, the animal belongs to the LORD and must be offered. Unlike the animals of verses 11-13, it cannot be redeemed; the next verse forbids even exchanging it.

records.heading: Vows of animals, houses and fields

records.source: לֹ֣א יַחֲלִיפֶ֗נּוּ וְלֹֽא־יָמִ֥יר אֹת֛וֹ ט֥וֹב בְּרָ֖ע אוֹ־רַ֣ע בְּט֑וֹב וְאִם־הָמֵ֨ר יָמִ֤יר בְּהֵמָה֙ בִּבְהֵמָ֔ה וְהָֽיָה־ה֥וּא וּתְמוּרָת֖וֹ יִֽהְיֶה־קֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: Not he will replace it and not he will exchange it, good for bad or bad for good; and if indeed he exchanges an animal for an animal, and will be it and its substitute holy.
pieces: The owner must not swap it or put another in its place, a good animal for a poor one or a poor one for a good one. If they do replace one animal with another, both the first animal and the one put in its place will be holy.

L.10: He shall not replace it and shall not exchange it, a good for a bad or a bad for a good; and if he does indeed exchange animal for animal, then it and its substitute shall be holy.

R.10: The owner must not trade it for another animal, a better one for a worse one or a worse one for a better one. If they do trade, then both animals will belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: replace ... exchange: no substitute of any kind
decisions.reason: Two verbs are used, both meaning to put one thing in place of another. Together they rule out any swap, whether to the giver's loss or gain. The second verb returns in verse 33 for the tithe of animals.

decisions.choice: it and its substitute will be holy: the attempt costs the owner both
decisions.reason: Whoever tries to exchange a vowed animal loses both: the first stays holy and the second becomes holy as well.

decisions.choice: will belong to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable explains "holy" here as belonging to the LORD, the sense of m2 in verse 9.

records.source: וְאִם֙ כָּל־בְּהֵמָ֣ה טְמֵאָ֔ה אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹא־יַקְרִ֧יבוּ מִמֶּ֛נָּה קָרְבָּ֖ן לַֽיהוָ֑ה וְהֶֽעֱמִ֥יד אֶת־הַבְּהֵמָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י הַכֹּהֵֽן׃
records.gloss: And if any animal unclean which not people bring near of it [as] an offering to Yahweh, and he will station the animal before the priest,
pieces: If the vow is of an unclean animal, of the kind that may not be presented as an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the animal is to be brought before the priest,

L.11: And if [it is] any unclean animal, of which [people] do not bring near an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, then he shall set the animal before the priest,

R.11: Someone may promise an unclean animal, one that cannot be offered to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then the animal must be brought to the priest.

decisions.choice: unclean animal: one not allowed on the altar
decisions.reason: "Unclean" here means an animal that may not be sacrificed, such as a donkey or a camel (11:4; Exodus 13:13). It could still be vowed, and its value was given to the sanctuary instead (verses 12-13).

records.source: וְהֶעֱרִ֤יךְ הַכֹּהֵן֙ אֹתָ֔הּ בֵּ֥ין ט֖וֹב וּבֵ֣ין רָ֑ע כְּעֶרְכְּךָ֥ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן כֵּ֥ן יִהְיֶֽה׃
records.gloss: and will value the priest it, between good and between bad; according to your valuation, the priest, so it will be.
pieces: and the priest will set its value according to whether it is good or poor. The value he sets will stand.

L.12: and the priest shall value it, whether good or bad; according to your valuation, O priest, so it shall be.

R.12: The priest will decide how much it is worth, whether it is a good animal or a poor one. The price the priest sets is final.

decisions.choice: according to your valuation, priest: the priest's value is final
decisions.reason: The fixed word "your valuation" (verse 2) here stands next to "the priest", and may be read as addressed to him ("your valuation, O priest") or as "the valuation of the priest". Either way, the value the priest sets is the one that holds.

decisions.choice: between good and bad: whatever its quality
decisions.reason: The phrase covers the whole range from best to worst; the priest values the animal as it is, as in verse 14 for a house.

decisions.choice: O priest
decisions.reason: Literal shows the most direct reading of the Hebrew, where "your valuation" is followed by "the priest"; see m1.

records.source: וְאִם־גָּאֹ֖ל יִגְאָלֶ֑נָּה וְיָסַ֥ף חֲמִישִׁת֖וֹ עַל־עֶרְכֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And if indeed he redeems it, and he will add its fifth to your valuation.
pieces: If the owner does redeem it, they must pay the valuation and a fifth more.

L.13: And if he does indeed redeem it, then he shall add its fifth to your valuation.

R.13: If the owner wants to buy the animal back, they must pay the set price plus one fifth more.

decisions.choice: redeem: buy back what was given
decisions.reason: To redeem is to buy back something that has passed to another, as family land is redeemed in 25:25. The owner may take back the unclean animal by paying its value to the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: add its fifth: pay twenty percent above the value
decisions.reason: The added fifth is the same as in the guilt offering (5:16, 24) and the redeemed tithe (verse 31). It makes redeeming a vowed gift costlier than leaving it with the sanctuary.

decisions.choice: buy back
decisions.reason: Readable says "buy back" for "redeem" through this chapter.

records.source: וְאִ֗ישׁ כִּֽי־יַקְדִּ֨שׁ אֶת־בֵּית֥וֹ קֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְהֶעֱרִיכוֹ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן בֵּ֥ין ט֖וֹב וּבֵ֣ין רָ֑ע כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲרִ֥יךְ אֹת֛וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן כֵּ֥ן יָקֽוּם׃
records.gloss: And a man, when he consecrates his house [as] holy to Yahweh, and will value it the priest between good and between bad; as will value it the priest, so it will stand.
pieces: When {{gender:anyone|any man}} consecrates a house as holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the priest is to judge whether it is in good or poor condition and set its value. The value the priest sets will stand.

L.14: And {{gender:a person|a man}}, when he consecrates his house [as] holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, then the priest shall value it, whether good or bad; as the priest values it, so it shall stand.

R.14: Someone may set apart their house as holy for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then the priest will decide how much it is worth, whether it is a good house or a poor one. The price he sets will not change.

decisions.choice: consecrates as holy: gives over to the LORD
decisions.reason: To consecrate is to make holy, here to hand property over to the LORD as a gift to the sanctuary, as in 8:10. The house would then belong to the sanctuary, or the owner could redeem it (verse 15).

decisions.choice: a man: anyone who owns a house
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, the law is for any owner, man or woman.

decisions.choice: a house / their house
decisions.reason: Balanced avoids the pronoun with "a house"; Readable uses "their" for the owner, who may be a man or a woman. Literal keeps "his".

records.source: וְאִ֨ם־הַמַּקְדִּ֔ישׁ יִגְאַ֖ל אֶת־בֵּית֑וֹ וְ֠יָסַף חֲמִישִׁ֧ית כֶּֽסֶף־עֶרְכְּךָ֛ עָלָ֖יו וְהָ֥יָה לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And if the one consecrating will redeem his house, and he will add a fifth of [the] silver of your valuation to it, and it will be his.
pieces: If the one who consecrated the house wants to redeem it, they must pay its value in silver and a fifth more, and it will be theirs again.

L.15: And if the one who consecrated [it] redeems his house, then he shall add a fifth of the silver of your valuation to it, and it shall be his.

R.15: If the owner wants to buy the house back, they must pay the set price plus one fifth more. Then it will be theirs again.

decisions.choice: add a fifth of the silver: pay the value plus twenty percent
decisions.reason: As in verse 13, the one who redeems pays the value set by the priest and adds a fifth. "Silver" is the payment, weighed out (verse 3).

decisions.choice: theirs again
decisions.reason: "It will be his" means the house returns to its owner; Balanced and Readable add "again".

records.source: וְאִ֣ם׀מִשְּׂדֵ֣ה אֲחֻזָּת֗וֹ יַקְדִּ֥ישׁ אִישׁ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה עֶרְכְּךָ֖ לְפִ֣י זַרְע֑וֹ זֶ֚רַע חֹ֣מֶר שְׂעֹרִ֔ים בַּחֲמִשִּׁ֖ים שֶׁ֥קֶל כָּֽסֶף׃
records.gloss: And if some of [the] field of his possession a man consecrates to Yahweh, and will be your valuation according to the mouth of its seed: seed of a homer of barley for fifty shekel[s] of silver.
pieces: If {{gender:anyone|any man}} consecrates to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} part of a field that is their family's land, its value will follow the seed needed to sow it: fifty shekels of silver for {{units:about 6 bushels|a homer}} of barley seed.

L.16: And if {{gender:a person|a man}} consecrates to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} some of the field of his possession, then your valuation shall be according to its seed: seed of a homer of barley at fifty shekels of silver.

R.16: Someone may give part of their family's land to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then the price will depend on how much seed it takes to plant it. The price is fifty shekels of silver for every {{units:about 6 bushels|a homer}} of barley seed.

decisions.choice: the field of his possession: inherited family land
decisions.reason: "Possession" is land held as a family's lasting share, which could not be sold for good and returned to the family in the Jubilee (25:10, 23-28). The field given here is that kind of land; a bought field is treated in verses 22-24.

decisions.choice: homer: the largest dry measure
decisions.reason: A homer was a dry measure, about 6 bushels (roughly 220 liters), perhaps first the load a donkey could carry. It was ten ephahs (Ezekiel 45:11).

decisions.choice: according to its seed: by the amount of seed needed to sow it
decisions.reason: The field is valued by its size, measured by the seed it takes to sow it: fifty shekels for each homer of seed. Verses 17-18 show that this is the price for the full fifty years between Jubilees, about a shekel a year. The phrase could instead mean the harvest the field yields, but "seed of a homer" points to sowing.

decisions.choice: family's land
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "his possession" is: the land a family holds by inheritance (m1).

records.source: אִם־מִשְּׁנַ֥ת הַיֹּבֵ֖ל יַקְדִּ֣ישׁ שָׂדֵ֑הוּ כְּעֶרְכְּךָ֖ יָקֽוּם׃
records.gloss: If from [the] year of the Jubilee he consecrates his field, according to your valuation it will stand.
pieces: If the field is consecrated from the Year of Jubilee onward, the full valuation will stand.

L.17: If he consecrates his field from the year of the Jubilee, it shall stand according to your valuation.

R.17: If the field is given in the Year of Jubilee, the full price stays the same.

decisions.choice: from the year of the Jubilee: at the start of the fifty-year cycle
decisions.reason: The Jubilee was the fiftieth year, when family land went back to its owners (25:10-13). A field given right after it would stay with the sanctuary for the whole cycle, so the full value applies.

decisions.choice: full
decisions.reason: The point is that nothing is taken off (compare verse 18); Balanced and Readable add "full".

records.source: וְאִם־אַחַ֣ר הַיֹּבֵל֮ יַקְדִּ֣ישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ֒ וְחִשַּׁב־ל֨וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אֶת־הַכֶּ֗סֶף עַל־פִּ֤י הַשָּׁנִים֙ הַנּ֣וֹתָרֹ֔ת עַ֖ד שְׁנַ֣ת הַיֹּבֵ֑ל וְנִגְרַ֖ע מֵֽעֶרְכֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And if after the Jubilee he consecrates his field, and will calculate for him the priest the silver according to the mouth of the years that remain until [the] year of the Jubilee, and it will be deducted from your valuation.
pieces: But if the field is consecrated after the Jubilee, the priest will work out the price by the years left until the next Year of Jubilee, and the valuation will be reduced to match.

L.18: But if he consecrates his field after the Jubilee, then the priest shall calculate the silver for him according to the years that remain until the year of the Jubilee, and it shall be deducted from your valuation.

R.18: But the field may be given some years after the Year of Jubilee. Then the priest will figure out the price by counting the years left until the next Jubilee. The price will be less.

decisions.choice: according to the years that remain: a price in proportion to the time
decisions.reason: The field returns to its family in the Jubilee (verse 21), so the sanctuary holds it only for the years left until then. The price is lowered in proportion, much as the price of land in a sale is set by the years to the Jubilee (25:15-16).

decisions.choice: the next
decisions.reason: The years are counted to the coming Jubilee; Balanced and Readable add "next".

records.source: וְאִם־גָּאֹ֤ל יִגְאַל֙ אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה הַמַּקְדִּ֖ישׁ אֹת֑וֹ וְ֠יָסַף חֲמִשִׁ֧ית כֶּֽסֶף־עֶרְכְּךָ֛ עָלָ֖יו וְקָ֥ם לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And if indeed he redeems the field, the one consecrating it, and he will add a fifth of [the] silver of your valuation to it, and it will stand to him.
pieces: If the one who consecrated the field does redeem it, they must pay its value in silver and a fifth more, and it will remain theirs.

L.19: And if the one who consecrated it does indeed redeem the field, then he shall add a fifth of the silver of your valuation to it, and it shall stand [as] his.

R.19: If the owner wants to buy the field back, they must pay the price plus one fifth more. Then the field will be theirs again.

decisions.choice: add a fifth: as for a house
decisions.reason: The rule of verse 15 applies to a field: the value plus a fifth.

decisions.choice: it will stand to him: it will be confirmed as his
decisions.reason: The verb "stand" means to be firm or settled; the field is his once more.

records.source: וְאִם־לֹ֤א יִגְאַל֙ אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה וְאִם־מָכַ֥ר אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה לְאִ֣ישׁ אַחֵ֑ר לֹ֥א יִגָּאֵ֖ל עֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: And if not he redeems the field, and if he has sold the field to another man, not it will be redeemed again.
pieces: But if they do not redeem the field, or if the field has been sold to someone else, it can never again be redeemed.

L.20: But if he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed any more.

R.20: But if the owner does not buy the field back, or if it has been sold to someone else, it can never be bought back.

decisions.choice: he has sold: who sold the field is not certain
decisions.reason: "He has sold" may mean the owner, who sold to someone else a field he had already given to the LORD and so had no right to sell. It may also mean the priest or the sanctuary, which sold the use of the field to another. In either case the first owner loses the right to buy it back.

decisions.choice: someone else
decisions.reason: "Another man" means any other person; Balanced and Readable say "someone else".

decisions.choice: has been sold
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the passive so as not to decide who sold it (m1). Literal keeps "he has sold".

records.source: וְהָיָ֨ה הַשָּׂדֶ֜ה בְּצֵאת֣וֹ בַיֹּבֵ֗ל קֹ֛דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֖ה כִּשְׂדֵ֣ה הַחֵ֑רֶם לַכֹּהֵ֖ן תִּהְיֶ֥ה אֲחֻזָּתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And will be the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, holy to Yahweh, like the field of the devoted thing; to the priest will be his possession.
pieces: When the field is released in the Jubilee, it will be holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, like a field that is devoted to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. It will belong to the priest as his own land.

L.21: And the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, like the field of the devoted thing; it shall be the priest's possession.

R.21: In the Year of Jubilee, when land goes back to its owners, this field will belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It will be like land that is given to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} forever. It will belong to the priest.

decisions.choice: when it goes out in the Jubilee: when land is released
decisions.reason: In the Jubilee land "goes out" from the one who bought it and returns to its family (25:28, 31). This field does not go back to its first owner but passes for good to the LORD.

decisions.choice: the devoted thing: something given over to the LORD for good
decisions.reason: This is the first use in Leviticus of the word explained at verse 28: something devoted wholly and finally to the LORD. A devoted field becomes the priests' (Numbers 18:14; Ezekiel 44:29).

decisions.choice: to the priest: the priesthood holds it
decisions.reason: "The priest" most likely means the priests as a body, who hold the field as a possession in place of the family that gave it up.

decisions.choice: when land goes back to its owners
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "goes out in the Jubilee" means (m1).

records.source: וְאִם֙ אֶת־שְׂדֵ֣ה מִקְנָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֕ר לֹ֖א מִשְּׂדֵ֣ה אֲחֻזָּת֑וֹ יַקְדִּ֖ישׁ לַֽיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And if a field of his purchase, which [is] not of [the] field of his possession, he consecrates to Yahweh,
pieces: If someone consecrates to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a field they have bought, which is not part of their family's land,

L.22: And if he consecrates to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a field that he bought, which [is] not of the field of his possession,

R.22: Someone may give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a field they bought, which is not part of their family's land.

decisions.choice: a bought field: land held only until the Jubilee
decisions.reason: A field bought from another family was held only until the Jubilee, when it went back to its owner (25:13-16, 28). The buyer owned only its use for the years remaining, and that is all he could give.

records.source: וְחִשַּׁב־ל֣וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֗ן אֵ֚ת מִכְסַ֣ת הָֽעֶרְכְּךָ֔ עַ֖ד שְׁנַ֣ת הַיֹּבֵ֑ל וְנָתַ֤ן אֶת־הָעֶרְכְּךָ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא קֹ֖דֶשׁ לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: and will calculate for him the priest the amount of your valuation until [the] year of the Jubilee, and he will give your valuation on that day, a holy thing to Yahweh.
pieces: the priest will work out the amount of the valuation up to the Year of Jubilee, and that person must pay the valuation on the same day as a holy gift to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.23: then the priest shall calculate for him the amount of your valuation up to the year of the Jubilee, and he shall give your valuation on that day, [as] holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.23: The priest will figure out its price, up to the Year of Jubilee. The person must pay that price on the same day. The money is a holy gift to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: he will give on that day: the giver pays the value at once
decisions.reason: With a bought field the sanctuary does not hold the land; the one who gave it pays its value, worked out for the years to the Jubilee, on the day of the gift. The payment itself is holy to the LORD.

records.source: בִּשְׁנַ֤ת הַיּוֹבֵל֙ יָשׁ֣וּב הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר קָנָ֖הוּ מֵאִתּ֑וֹ לַאֲשֶׁר־ל֖וֹ אֲחֻזַּ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: In [the] year of the Jubilee will return the field to whom he bought it from with him, to whom [belongs] the possession of the land.
pieces: In the Year of Jubilee the field will go back to the one from whom it was bought, the one whose family land it is.

L.24: In the year of the Jubilee the field shall return to the one from whom he bought it, to the one to whom the possession of the land [belongs].

R.24: In the Year of Jubilee the field will go back to the person who sold it, whose family the land belongs to.

decisions.choice: the field returns to its owner: the Jubilee law holds
decisions.reason: The rule of 25:10, 13, 28 applies even to a field given to the sanctuary: it goes back to the family that holds it as its possession. Family land could not pass out of a family for good by sale (25:23).

records.source: וְכָל־עֶרְכְּךָ֔ יִהְיֶ֖ה בְּשֶׁ֣קֶל הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים גֵּרָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֥ה הַשָּֽׁקֶל׃ס
records.gloss: And every your valuation will be by [the] shekel of the holy place; twenty gerah[s] will be the shekel.
pieces: Every valuation is to be by the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.

L.25: And every valuation of yours shall be by the shekel of the sanctuary; twenty gerahs shall be the shekel.

R.25: Every price must be figured by the official shekel used at the holy tent. That shekel weighs twenty gerahs.

decisions.choice: twenty gerahs: the sanctuary shekel defined
decisions.reason: The gerah was the smallest unit of weight, about half a gram, a twentieth of a shekel. The same definition is given in Exodus 30:13, Numbers 3:47 and Ezekiel 45:12. On the shekel, see verse 3.

records.source: אַךְ־בְּכ֞וֹר אֲשֶׁר־יְבֻכַּ֤ר לַֽיהוָה֙ בִּבְהֵמָ֔ה לֹֽא־יַקְדִּ֥ישׁ אִ֖ישׁ אֹת֑וֹ אִם־שׁ֣וֹר אִם־שֶׂ֔ה לַֽיהוָ֖ה הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: Nevertheless a firstborn which is born first to Yahweh among livestock, not a man will consecrate it; whether an ox or a sheep, to Yahweh it [belongs].
pieces: But {{gender:no one|no man}} may consecrate the firstborn of an animal, since a firstborn already belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Whether it is from the cattle or the flock, it is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s.

L.26: Nevertheless a firstborn among livestock, which is born first to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} — {{gender:a person|a man}} shall not consecrate it; whether ox or sheep, it [belongs] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.26: But no one may promise to give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the first animal born to a cow or a sheep. It already belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a firstborn belongs to the LORD already
decisions.reason: Every firstborn male of the herd and flock belonged to the LORD from birth (Exodus 13:2, 12; 34:19; Numbers 18:17). It could not be offered by vow, because one cannot give what is already his.

decisions.choice: ox or sheep: cattle or the flock
decisions.reason: The first word is a head of cattle; the second is one animal of the flock, sheep or goat.

decisions.choice: since / already
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that "which is born first to the LORD" gives the reason it cannot be consecrated.

records.heading: Firstborn, devoted things and tithes

records.source: וְאִ֨ם בַּבְּהֵמָ֤ה הַטְּמֵאָה֙ וּפָדָ֣ה בְעֶרְכֶּ֔ךָ וְיָסַ֥ף חֲמִשִׁת֖וֹ עָלָ֑יו וְאִם־לֹ֥א יִגָּאֵ֖ל וְנִמְכַּ֥ר בְּעֶרְכֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And if among the unclean livestock, and he will ransom [it] by your valuation and he will add its fifth to it; and if not it is redeemed, and it will be sold by your valuation.
pieces: If it is an unclean animal, the owner may buy it back at its valuation, adding a fifth to it. If it is not redeemed, it is to be sold at its valuation.

L.27: And if [it is] among the unclean livestock, then he shall ransom [it] by your valuation and add its fifth to it; and if it is not redeemed, then it shall be sold by your valuation.

R.27: If the first animal born is unclean, the owner may buy it back. They must pay the set price plus one fifth more. If they do not buy it back, it must be sold at the set price.

decisions.choice: among the unclean livestock: an unclean firstborn
decisions.reason: Following verse 26, this most likely means the firstborn of an unclean animal. Exodus 13:13 and 34:20 have the firstborn donkey redeemed with a lamb or else its neck broken; here a payment of silver is allowed, or the animal is sold and the price goes to the sanctuary. The verse may instead be a general rule for unclean animals.

decisions.choice: ransom ... redeem: two words for buying back
decisions.reason: The first verb means to ransom or set free by payment; the second is the word used for redeeming in verses 13-20. Here they mean the same.

decisions.choice: the first animal born
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject, following m1.

records.source: אַךְ־כָּל־חֵ֡רֶם אֲשֶׁ֣ר יַחֲרִם֩ אִ֨ישׁ לַֽיהוָ֜ה מִכָּל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֗וֹ מֵאָדָ֤ם וּבְהֵמָה֙ וּמִשְּׂדֵ֣ה אֲחֻזָּת֔וֹ לֹ֥א יִמָּכֵ֖ר וְלֹ֣א יִגָּאֵ֑ל כָּל־חֵ֕רֶם קֹֽדֶשׁ־קָֽדָשִׁ֥ים ה֖וּא לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Nevertheless every devoted thing which a man devotes to Yahweh, from all that [is] his, from humankind and livestock and from [the] field of his possession, not it will be sold and not it will be redeemed; every devoted thing [is] most holy to Yahweh.
pieces: But anything that {{gender:anyone|any man}} devotes to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from what they own, whether human or animal or a field they hold as family land, may not be sold and may not be bought back. All that is devoted is most holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.28: Nevertheless, every devoted thing that {{gender:a person|a man}} devotes to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from all that he has, of human and of animal and of the field of his possession, shall not be sold and shall not be redeemed; every devoted thing [is] a most holy [thing] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.28: But someone may give something to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as fully devoted to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. It may be a person, an animal, or family land. It can never be sold or bought back. Everything devoted in this way is very holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: devoted thing: given over to the LORD wholly and for good
decisions.reason: The noun and its verb describe something taken out of human use and handed over to the LORD with no way back. Unlike a vow (verses 2-27), it cannot be redeemed. A devoted thing belonged to the sanctuary and the priests (verse 21; Numbers 18:14; Ezekiel 44:29). In war the same word is used for the enemy and their goods given over to the LORD by destruction (Numbers 21:2-3; Deuteronomy 7:2; Joshua 6:17-21; 1 Samuel 15:3).

decisions.choice: of human: persons under the owner's control
decisions.reason: The verse lists what an owner might devote: people, animals and land. The people are most likely those in his household under his authority, such as slaves; the verse does not say what became of them, and verse 29 deals with a different case.

decisions.choice: most holy: of the highest holiness
decisions.reason: "Holy of holies" is the strongest form of "holy", used of the most sacred offerings (2:3). A devoted thing belongs to the LORD in the fullest way.

decisions.choice: fully devoted to him
decisions.reason: Readable explains "devote" as giving something to the LORD fully, in line with m1.

records.source: כָּל־חֵ֗רֶם אֲשֶׁ֧ר יָחֳרַ֛ם מִן־הָאָדָ֖ם לֹ֣א יִפָּדֶ֑ה מ֖וֹת יוּמָֽת׃
records.gloss: Every devoted person who is devoted from humankind not will be ransomed; surely he will be put to death.
pieces: When a human being has been placed under the ban for destruction, no ransom may be paid for them; they must be put to death.

L.29: Every devoted [person] who is devoted from humankind shall not be ransomed; he shall surely be put to death.

R.29: If a person has been devoted to destruction, no one can pay to set that person free. That person must be put to death.

decisions.choice: devoted from humankind: a person placed under the ban by judgment
decisions.reason: The verb is passive: the person "is devoted", not by a private vow (verses 2-8, where a person could always be redeemed) but most likely by a judgment under God's law. The law says that whoever sacrifices to other gods is to be devoted to destruction (Exodus 22:19), and a whole town that turns to other gods is to be devoted in the same way (Deuteronomy 13). The word is also used for enemies devoted in war (Numbers 21:2-3; Joshua 6:17; 1 Samuel 15:3). The verse does not say who carried out the death, nor does it allow an owner to put someone to death by a vow. What exactly it covers is not certain.

decisions.choice: not ransomed ... surely put to death
decisions.reason: "Ransomed" is the verb of verse 27. A devoted person cannot be bought free as a vowed person can. "Surely put to death" is the form used for the death penalty elsewhere in the law (20:2, 9-16).

decisions.choice: placed under the ban for destruction
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out that this is the ban (m1), and that the passive verb describes a person put in that state, not an offering.

decisions.choice: no one can pay to set that person free
decisions.reason: Readable explains "ransomed".

records.source: וְכָל־מַעְשַׂ֨ר הָאָ֜רֶץ מִזֶּ֤רַע הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ מִפְּרִ֣י הָעֵ֔ץ לַיהוָ֖ה ה֑וּא קֹ֖דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And all [the] tithe of the land, of [the] seed of the land, of [the] fruit of the tree, to Yahweh it [belongs]; a holy thing to Yahweh.
pieces: All the tithe of the land belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, both grain from what is sown and fruit from the trees. It is holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.30: And every tithe of the land, of the seed of the land [and] of the fruit of the tree, it [belongs] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; [it is] holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.30: A tenth of everything the land produces belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This includes grain from the fields and fruit from the trees. It is holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: tithe: a tenth part
decisions.reason: The word means a tenth. Abram gave a tenth to Melchizedek (Genesis 14:20) and Jacob promised a tenth to God (Genesis 28:22). The law gives the tithe to the Levites for their service (Numbers 18:21-24) and also tells how it was to be eaten in a festival (Deuteronomy 14:22-29). Like the firstborn, it already belongs to the LORD and is not a vow.

decisions.choice: the seed of the land, the fruit of the tree: grain and fruit
decisions.reason: "Seed" here is what grows from sowing, the grain of the fields; "fruit of the tree" covers the produce of trees and vines, such as olives and grapes (Deuteronomy 14:23).

decisions.choice: a tenth
decisions.reason: Readable says what "tithe" means; Literal and Balanced keep the word.

records.source: וְאִם־גָּאֹ֥ל יִגְאַ֛ל אִ֖ישׁ מִמַּֽעַשְׂר֑וֹ חֲמִשִׁית֖וֹ יֹסֵ֥ף עָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And if indeed he redeems, a man, some of his tithe, its fifth he will add to it.
pieces: If {{gender:anyone|any man}} wants to redeem any of their tithe, they must add a fifth to its value.

L.31: And if {{gender:a person|a man}} does indeed redeem some of his tithe, he shall add its fifth to it.

R.31: If someone wants to buy back part of their tenth, they must pay its value plus one fifth more.

decisions.choice: redeem some of his tithe: keep the produce and pay its value plus a fifth
decisions.reason: An owner could keep part of his grain or fruit tithe by paying its value and a fifth more, as with vowed gifts (verses 13, 15, 19). Animals of the tithe could not be redeemed (verse 33).

records.source: וְכָל־מַעְשַׂ֤ר בָּקָר֙ וָצֹ֔אן כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲבֹ֖ר תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑בֶט הָֽעֲשִׂירִ֕י יִֽהְיֶה־קֹּ֖דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And all [the] tithe of [the] herd and [the] flock, all that passes under the rod, the tenth will be holy to Yahweh.
pieces: As for the herd and the flock, of all the animals that pass under the rod as they are counted, every tenth one will be holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.32: And every tithe of herd and flock, all that passes under the rod, the tenth shall be holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.32: The shepherd counts the cattle, sheep and goats as they walk under his staff. Every tenth animal will belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as holy.

decisions.choice: passes under the rod: is counted by the shepherd
decisions.reason: A shepherd counted his animals as they went one by one beneath his rod or staff (Jeremiah 33:13; Ezekiel 20:37). Every tenth animal that passed was the LORD's, whatever it was like, so the choice was left to the count and not to the owner (verse 33).

decisions.choice: herd and flock: cattle, and sheep and goats
decisions.reason: The herd is cattle; the flock is sheep and goats together, as in 1:2.

decisions.choice: as they are counted / The shepherd counts
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what passing under the rod is for (m1).

records.source: לֹ֧א יְבַקֵּ֛ר בֵּֽין־ט֥וֹב לָרַ֖ע וְלֹ֣א יְמִירֶ֑נּוּ וְאִם־הָמֵ֣ר יְמִירֶ֔נּוּ וְהָֽיָה־ה֧וּא וּתְמוּרָת֛וֹ יִֽהְיֶה־קֹ֖דֶשׁ לֹ֥א יִגָּאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Not he will inspect between good and bad and not he will exchange it; and if indeed he exchanges it, and will be it and its substitute holy; not it will be redeemed.
pieces: The owner is not to look over the animals to sort good from poor, and must not exchange one for another. If they do make an exchange, the animal and the one put in its place will both be holy, and neither can be redeemed.'"

L.33: He shall not inspect [whether it is] good or bad, and he shall not exchange it; and if he does indeed exchange it, then it and its substitute shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.'"

R.33: The owner must not look to see if the animal is good or bad, and must not trade it for another. If they do trade, both animals will belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as holy. Neither one can be bought back.'"

decisions.choice: inspect: look over in order to choose
decisions.reason: The verb means to examine or seek out, as a shepherd looks over his flock (Ezekiel 34:11-12). The owner is not to pick which animals pass tenth, good or poor.

decisions.choice: exchange ... it and its substitute: the rule of verse 10
decisions.reason: The penalty for swapping is the same as for a vowed animal (verse 10): both become holy. And a tithe animal cannot be redeemed, unlike the grain tithe (verse 31).

decisions.choice: will belong to the LORD as holy
decisions.reason: Readable explains "holy" here as belonging to the LORD, as in verse 10.

records.source: אֵ֣לֶּה הַמִּצְוֺ֗ת אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בְּהַ֖ר סִינָֽי׃
records.gloss: These [are] the commandments which commanded Yahweh Moses to [the] sons of Israel on [the] mountain of Sinai.
pieces: These are the commandments {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} laid on Moses for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, on Mount Sinai.

L.34: These [are] the commandments that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded Moses for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel on Mount Sinai.

R.34: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave all these commands to Moses on Mount Sinai, for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: these are the commandments: the close of the book
decisions.reason: The verse ends this chapter and Leviticus as a whole, as 26:46 closed the laws before it. "On Mount Sinai" places all of it at the mountain, as 7:38 and 25:1 do, before Israel sets out in Numbers.

decisions.choice: commandments: the instructions God gave
decisions.reason: The word is the general term for what God commands, from the same root as the verb "commanded" in this verse (4:2; 26:3).
